source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - Carlos Lopez x Harry Edmonds — Follow Up

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title and no setter named on the call. The route was inbound and self-served: "I know he offers classes. Let me start through there... a few clicks and then, you know, did the little thing online. And next thing you know, I had the call set up." The rep worked from the written application: "I got your application. I got all those details."

prospect.name: Carlos Lopez
prospect.location: United States (state not stated); grew up in Pereira, Colombia, with family from Medellín and military school in Santa Marta
prospect.family_status: Married; two daughters, one at college and one finishing her freshman year of high school. First in his family to be college educated.
prospect.training_background: Fit through his teens playing soccer in Colombia and attending military school, then overweight through his twenties and half his thirties, peaking near 250 lb. Has trained seriously and consistently for close to ten years and now sits at a self-reported 190-195 lb. Trains most mornings, prefers training to the point of nausea, has had to teach himself to take rest days. Ran his first half marathon in February. Plays a lot of golf. Programming is entirely self-assembled from YouTube and is predominantly bodybuilding-style pushing weight; describes his kettlebell knowledge as a 2 or 3 out of 10.
prospect.medical: Two recent musculoskeletal injuries, both self-attributed to unsupervised training. Hamstring tweaked squatting three days before the call — "on today is Thursday, I think it was Monday, I tweaked my hamstring squatting. And honestly, that's what led me to like, you know what, it's time." Shoulder tweaked a few months earlier, with recurring pain whenever he trains chest: "I have tried to do more chest, but then it starts hurting my shoulders." Also reports a pattern: "have dealt with a few injuries because I'm not doing it right." Consults a friend who is a physical therapist. No clinician clearance discussed on the call.

signals: Adopted the good-to-great frame himself when the rep offered it: "Sounds like you want to go from good to great" — "Yeah, pretty much. That's a good way to put it." Self-scored 7.5-8 out of 10

Openly motivated by appearance as well as function — "I'm not going to lie and say 50-50, but more probably like 60-40, 60 vanity, 40 health" — and by refusing decline: "father time is undefeated. I understand that, but I'm willing to put up the fight for as long as possible"

Diverges from the profile on one dimension that matters: price was a real barrier, not a quality signal. "Yeah, it's a lot, honestly. I didn't think it was going to be that high" and a consumer finance application was declined during the call.

goals.text: Get expert guidance on what he specifically should be doing rather than cookie-cutter programming
Break the plateau he has hit with self-directed bodybuilding-style training
Stay flexible as he ages, particularly for golf
Be injury-free and stop hurting himself training wrong
Still be hiking, swimming and running at 60 — refuse the idea that ageing means decline
Muscle tone and a six-pack — "be in the best shape of my life into my 40s"
A roadmap he understands, with the knowledge to keep going after the six months
Balance across strength, flexibility and cardio rather than gaining one at the cost of another

pains.text: Plateaued — "I kind of hit a plateau and I'm like, I need help to get to that next point"
Repeatedly injuring himself through self-directed training, most recently a hamstring three days before the call
Shoulder pain that recurs whenever he trains chest, blocking balanced development
Everything he does is bodybuilding-style — strong but tight, losing flexibility
Assembling his own programme from YouTube with no way to know what is right for him
Competing family financial commitments — a daughter at college and household expenses
Historically unable to take rest days; had to train himself out of it after an injury

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, it's a lot, honestly. I didn't think it was going to be that high, Harry. Right now, you know, my gym membership is, I think, like 50 bucks a month.
objections.rep_response: Held the price and isolated properly — "Money aside, like the most important part, do you feel like we can actually like get you where you want to go?" — then moved to structure: an upfront default, a 50/50 split within 90 days, and a live Klarna financing check. Took a partial financial picture (credit score, debt profile) but never asked about cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards or investments.

objections.raw_quote: I do want to have an opportunity to discuss it, you know, with my wife. And like I said, just look at everything holistically... we just need to make sure that we don't have anything big coming up that I would have to commit some more funds to.
objections.rep_response: None. The rep did not run any part of the spouse play — no name, no 'what would she say', no 'is this her input or your permission', no deposit-with-refund fallback. He replied "That's so good" and asked how long the prospect needed.

objections.raw_quote: I would probably need like, you know, maybe like a month or two to get things situated to where I can be like, well, here's the upfront or can you guys work with me, you know, three now and another three months, the remaining three or something like that.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the split structure as workable ("three down, three months, that's possible as long as the other three is done before halfway") and then escalated to third-party financing to remove the delay entirely.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Four structures surfaced. Upfront on a credit card as the default ("that's what most people do"). A 50/50 split — "three down, three months, that's possible as long as the other three is done before halfway." Klarna financing, applied for live on the call and declined. A second financing partner carrying interest: six payments of $1,200 ($7,200 total) or twelve payments of $650 ($7,800 total). The rep also stated there are no standard plans: "we don't have, like, set payment plans, if that makes sense."
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "our guarantee is that from your starting weight to the end of the six months, you will be swinging around a 20-pound heavier kettlebell in all of the movements, the main movements, obviously not like bicep curls, but snatches, all that sort of stuff."

prospect_financials.credit_score: Self-reported 800+; TransUnion 816 and Equifax 822 per Credit Karma. Only debt is a mortgage, refinanced roughly two months before the call. Declined by Klarna on the call, which both parties found inexplicable.

evidence: Explicit deferral with a timeline: "I couldn't commit to anything right now on this call" and "give me a good week... I think by Thursday next week, I should have a good idea which way I want to go"
Genuine intent stated repeatedly: "it is something that I'm serious about. And I would want to do" and "I do want to do it. I am serious about taking that next step"
Two live blockers unresolved — a spousal conversation and the household budget with a daughter at college

Counter-evidence on likelihood: the Klarna application was declined on the call despite an 800+ credit score, removing the zero-interest route he called "very attractive"; the remaining options carry $1,200-$1,800 of interest
No payment, no payment link that resulted in a transaction, and no onboarding call booked — Monday was mentioned as the target but never scheduled
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review household finances with his wife and revert by Thursday the following week; he travels to Orlando on the Monday and returns Tuesday night. Financing options left on the table at six payments of $1,200 or twelve of $650.

notable.note: The prospect is the clearest good-to-great case in the batch — the rep used the exact ICP phrase and the prospect adopted it — and the deal stalled on money, which the stated ICP assumes away. Three things a principal should see. First, the rep walked him into a live consumer credit application mid-call, framed as getting clarity on numbers rather than as applying for credit, and told him "it's a soft pull as well, so by the way, it won't affect anything." Klarna declined a man with an 822 Equifax score, which nobody could explain. Second, the fallback financing prices the $6,000 programme at $7,200 or $7,800. Third, and least defensible on process: the prospect said twice that he needed to talk to his wife and the spouse play was not run at any point — not one question about her, which is the single largest missed play in the batch. Also worth noting the prospect volunteered his exact credit bureau scores onto a recorded call.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion, worst from 00:18:00 onward. The rep's entire coaching walkthrough at 00:18:59-00:21:23 sits partly under the prospect's label, the isolate question at 00:25:48 ("Money aside, like the most important part, do you feel like we can actually get you where you want to go?") is attributed to Carlos when it is plainly the rep, and the long financing exchange at 00:27:00-00:29:22 runs both speakers together in undifferentiated blocks. Roles read from content throughout.
